llevar_vs_traer.overview: Both mean 'to carry/take/bring' but have opposite directional meaning, similar to English 'take' vs 'bring'.

llevar.english: to take, to carry (away from speaker)
llevar.direction: away from here / to another place
llevar.example: Llevo el pastel a la fiesta.
llevar.example_english: I'll take the cake to the party. (moving away from current location)

traer.example: ¿Tú no trajiste nada a la fiesta?
traer.example_english: Didn't you bring anything to the party?
traer.note: Irregular j-stem in preterite; ellos form drops the 'i' (trajeron, not trajieron)

restaurant_delivery_vocabulary.english: orders now / order now (delivery app-style phrase)

household_and_maintenance_vocabulary.spanish: Cuando no tiene mantenimiento se destruye.
household_and_maintenance_vocabulary.english: When it's not maintained, it gets destroyed.
